newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Former S.Korean general acquitted of sedition.
newsitem.headline: Former S.Korean general acquitted of sedition.

text.p: A former South Korean army chief who was jailed for his alleged role in the assassination of former president Park Chung-hee was on Thursday acquitted of sedition, court officials said.
Chung Seung-hwa, martial law commander at the time of the assassination in October 1979, was arrested two months later in a coup by then major-general Chun Doo Hwan.
The coup pushed Chun to the presidency in 1980. He stood down in 1988 when his army colleague Roh Tae-woo succeeded him for a six-year term.

A Seoul criminal court, reviewing a verdict handed out in 1980 by a military court controlled by Chun, on Thursday accepted Chung's argument that military investigators fabricated sedition charges by torturing him.
It cleared Chung of the military court verdict that he turned a blind eye to the assassination by Park's own intelligence chief.
The court officials said there was no evidence that Chung knew about the intelligence chief's assassination plan.
Chung, who was originally sentenced to 10 years in jail and stripped of his military rank, was freed after eight months when Chun suspended his sentence.

The review of Chung's verdict followed treason and mutiny convictions last year for Chun and Roh in connection with the 1979 coup and an army massacre the following year in the southwestern city of Kwangju, where about 200 people were killed.
Chun is now serving a life sentence and Roh a 17-year jail term.
Chung on Thursday regained his rights as a retired four-star general, including the right to be buried in the National Cemetery, the officals said.
